abstract: Psychiatric disorder is inherently heterogeneous and care is uniquely reliant on the interpretation of unstructured, longitudinal narratives that contain potential psychopathological cues. These contribute to the substantial variability in psychiatry, hindering standardized care. Can a psychiatry-specific large language model (LLM) assist clinicians in offering high-quality, consistent psychiatric care?
